title: HPLC fractionation with immunoassay of steroids from nipple aspirate fluid
author: Heinz, Chatterton
materials: To help prevent degradation of the aqueous sample, add 2 µL of protease inhibitor cocktail (Sigma P8340) (diluted 1:2 in DMSO) to the 0.5 mL Aq fractions and 1 µL to the 0.25 mL Aq fractions. Centrifuge the Aq fractions briefly to pool any moisture that may have condensed on the side walls while in the evaporator. Since some of the water in the Aq fraction may have evaporated and left the tube, measure the volume with a manual pipette, and add HPLC grade water as necessary to bring the Aq fraction back to the recorded volume of 0.5 mL or 0.25 mL. The Aq fractions can then be capped and stored at -20°C for no more than 1 month before assaying. The Aq fraction is represented in the graphical abstract as Fraction A in yellow.

steps.title: Add internal standards and extract steroids
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of the prepared internal‑standard cocktail (containing 250 ng each of DEX and PRED ACE) to every diluted sample, then add 1 mL of HPLC‑grade ethyl acetate:hexane (3:2) that has been equilibrated with HPLC‑grade water. Vortex the tube slowly, centrifuge for 5 min at ~2500 RCF, and transfer the top (organic) layer to a 12 × 75 mm polypropylene tube. Repeat the solvent addition, vortex, centrifuge and transfer two more times so that a total of 3 mL organic extract is collected, taking care to avoid any aqueous phase. Wear gloves and use filter tips throughout. Finally, evaporate any residual ethyl acetate:hexane from the aqueous fractions by placing the tubes in a 50 °C water bath under a gentle stream of nitrogen until the solvent is no longer detectable.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL internal‑standard cocktail (250 ng each DEX and PRED ACE).
Add 1 mL ethyl acetate:hexane (3:2) equilibrated with water.
Transfer top organic layer to 12 × 75 mm polypropylene tube; label.
Repeat solvent addition, vortex, centrifuge, transfer two more times (total 3 mL).
Evaporate residual solvent from aqueous fractions in 50 °C water bath under N₂.

steps.title: Prepare N2 evaporator to avoid contamination
steps.instruction: Replace the inline nitrogen‑evaporator filter at least every 6 months, wipe the inlet needles twice with methanol before insertion, avoid any needle‑sample contact, and turn on the nitrogen gas gently to prevent splashing.

substeps.instruction: Do not let needle touch sample.

steps.title: Add protease inhibitor and adjust aqueous fractions
steps.instruction: To each aqueous fraction add protease‑inhibitor cocktail (Sigma P8340 diluted 1:2 in DMSO): 2 µL for a 0.5 mL fraction or 1 µL for a 0.25 mL fraction. Centrifuge briefly to collect any condensed moisture, measure the current volume with a manual pipette, and add HPLC‑grade water to bring the volume back to the recorded 0.5 mL or 0.25 mL. Cap the tubes and store at –20 °C for no longer than one month before assay.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 µL inhibitor to 0.5 mL fractions (or 1 µL to 0.25 mL fractions).
Measure volume and add HPLC‑grade water to restore original volume.

steps.title: Assay aqueous fraction for target analytes
steps.instruction: Assay the aqueous fraction for dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate (DHEA‑S), total protein, and insulin‑like growth factor‑1 (IGF‑1). The lower limits of detection are 62.5 ng mL⁻¹ for DHEA‑S (Beckman‑Coulter DSL‑2700), 0.156 ng mL⁻¹ for IGF‑1, and 0.781 µg mL⁻¹ for protein. DHEA‑S and IGF‑1 are measured by radio‑immunoassay; protein is measured by a fluorescence‑based assay.

steps.title: Set up HPLC column and guard
steps.instruction: Install a Supelco Ascentis Express C18 column (Cat #53827‑U, 10 × 4.6 cm, 2.7 µm) together with a matching Supelco guard column (Cat #53508). Replace the guard column when the internal‑standard peak trails or shows a shoulder, and replace the analytical column when abnormally high pressure persists after system purging. Ensure the HPLC system is serviced according to the manufacturer’s schedule.

steps.title: Prepare HPLC buffers and wash solution
steps.instruction: Prepare three buffers using HPLC‑grade reagents: Buffer A = 60 % 15 mM phosphate buffer (pH 6.0), 20 % methanol, 20 % acetonitrile; Buffer B = 50 % acetonitrile, 50 % methanol; Wash solution = Buffer A without the phosphate salt. Make 4 L of Buffer A, store at 4 °C, and degas all buffers with an in‑line degasser to remove dissolved gases.

substeps.instruction: Mix Buffer A (60 % 15 mM phosphate pH 6, 20 % MeOH, 20 % ACN).
Prepare wash solution (Buffer A without salt).
Make 4 L Buffer A, store at 4 °C.
Degas all buffers with inline degasser.

steps.title: Reconstitute samples for HPLC injection
steps.instruction: Place the polypropylene tubes containing the organic extracts in a 50 °C water bath under nitrogen and evaporate the ethyl acetate:hexane completely (≈10–15 min). Re‑dissolve the residue in 40 µL Buffer B, vortex briefly, then add 60 µL HPLC‑grade water to reach a final volume of 100 µL. Program the autosampler to draw 75 µL for injection. Transfer the 100 µL solution to a glass polyspring insert labeled with the sample ID, place the insert into an amber HPLC vial, and seal with a silicone septum. Store the vials at 4 °C for up to a few days before fractionation.

substeps.instruction: Evaporate organic solvent at 50 °C under N₂ (10–15 min).
Re‑dissolve residue in 40 µL Buffer B; vortex.
Transfer to labeled glass polyspring insert.
Place insert in amber vial; seal with silicone septum.

steps.title: Initialize HPLC system and purge
steps.instruction: Turn on the HPLC system and set the column heater to 26.2 °C. Purge all system components with Buffer B until no bubbles remain, then purge the autosampler followed by the column. Prime the system with Buffer A until a stable baseline is observed, then re‑zero the UV detector.

substeps.instruction: Purge system with Buffer B until bubbles disappear.
Prime with Buffer A until baseline.

steps.title: Run HPLC gradient program and collect fractions
steps.instruction: Program the gradient as follows: 0–40 min 100 % Buffer A; 40–50 min linear to 50 % Buffer B; 50–55 min hold at 50 % Buffer B; 55–60 min linear to 100 % Buffer B; 60–65 min linear back to 100 % Buffer A; 65–75 min hold at 100 % Buffer A. Set the flow rate to 0.6 mL min⁻¹. Ensure the waste container is empty and large enough for the entire run.

substeps.instruction: 60–65 min: linear back to 100 % Buffer A.
Verify waste container is empty and sufficiently large.
